npcs.name: 卖古董的老板
npcs.role: a stallholder selling 'antiques' of every age
npcs.character: A born haggler, loud, cheerful; every price starts high.
knows: The clay 年兽 came from an old house in the 胡同

npcs.name: 卖旧书的大叔
npcs.role: a man selling old books who was robbed last month
npcs.character: Rueful, jokes about his own bad luck.
knows: Someone stole his books last month

explains.亡羊补牢: 东西丢了，再修门，以后就不会丢了。

npcs.name: 鬼市的卖家
npcs.role: a seller at the night market whose face you can never quite see
npcs.character: Whispers, laughs at nothing, sells only for riddles.

npcs.name: 卖茶壶的阿姨
npcs.character: Warm and quick; pours you a cup while you haggle.
knows: Prices at 潘家园 start high

npcs.name: 卖铜钱的爷爷
npcs.role: an old man with a cloth full of old coins
npcs.character: Slow, amused; knows every coin's emperor.
knows: Prices at 潘家园 start high

npcs.name: 卖扇子的姐姐
npcs.role: a young woman selling painted paper fans
npcs.character: Chatty, fans herself the whole time.
knows: Prices at 潘家园 start high

npcs.name: 卖鼻烟壶的老板
npcs.role: a man with tiny painted bottles under glass
npcs.character: Proud of every bottle; drops the price with a sigh.
knows: Prices at 潘家园 start high

npcs.name: 买老东西的老先生
npcs.role: an old collector who buys small old things
npcs.character: Peers at everything through his glasses; opens low, always.

nodes.translate: Hello! What would you like?
nodes.why: 古董摊: 灯笼 30 元. Say what you want and how many — 「两个包子」, 「一瓶水」 — ask 「多少钱？」 any time, and say 「不要了」 when that is all.

nodes.speaker: hero
nodes.translate: So this is 潘家园! So much stuff.
nodes.why: 潘家园 is Beijing's biggest antiques and flea market. Bargaining is expected: start at a third of the price.

nodes.translate: Last month my things were stolen.
Now I'm mending the door.
That's 亡羊补牢 — mending the pen after the sheep is gone.
nodes.why: A 成语 📌 with a story: better late than never — mend the pen after the first sheep is lost, and lose no more.

nodes.translate: Hello! Have a look at my antiques!

nodes.say: 这个年兽？是古董！两百块。
nodes.translate: This 年兽? A real antique! Two hundred.
nodes.why: 便宜点儿 — a bit cheaper. 真的假的 — really? Bargain: 「太贵了」, 「一百块行吗？」, or 「算了」 and walk away.

nodes.speaker: nianshou
nodes.say: 谢谢你！我是年兽。我们是朋友了！
nodes.translate: Thank you! I'm the 年兽. We're friends now!
nodes.why: The clay figure was a spirit from the lantern all along. The 年兽 of the New Year stories fears red — it has had a hard time among 潘家园's red cloths.

nodes.translate: Have a look at my antiques!

nodes.speaker: hero
nodes.translate: A little 年兽.

nodes.say: 你看，北京的地图！很老的！五十块。
nodes.translate: Look — a map of Beijing! Very old! Fifty.
nodes.why: 老 — old — is HSK 3: a small key line. Bargain! 「太贵了」, 「便宜一点」, 「三十块行吗？」 — or 「算了」 and walk away: he may call you back.

nodes.translate: Here you are!

nodes.say: 铃铛？我有很多铃铛。你要哪个？
nodes.translate: Bells? I have lots of bells. Which one?
This one? Take it — no charge.

words.explain: 一动就有声音的小东西。

nodes.translate: Heh heh… this is the ghost market. What do you want?

nodes.say: 长明灯？好。一个谜：洗手的时候，要它。它是什么？
nodes.translate: The lamp? Fine. A riddle: when you wash your hands, you need it. What is it?
nodes.why: The answer is 水: you wash your hands in water.

nodes.translate: Right! The lamp is yours.

nodes.speaker: hong-xiansheng
nodes.translate: Good or bad — it all comes down to a single thought.
nodes.why: 一念之间, “in the space of one thought”. This is his market, it seems.

words.explain: 晚上的市场，很奇怪的东西都有。

nodes.say: 你好！你看这个茶壶，很好看！八十块。
nodes.translate: Hello! Look at this teapot — lovely! Eighty.
nodes.why: Bargain! 「太贵了」, 「便宜一点」, a price of your own — 「二十块行吗？」 — or 「算了」: walk away, and they may call you back.

nodes.say: 谢谢！这个茶壶是你的了！
nodes.translate: Thank you! The teapot is yours!
Hello! Have a cup of tea!

nodes.say: 这是铜钱！很好的铜钱。二十五块。
nodes.translate: Copper coins! Fine old copper coins. Twenty-five.
nodes.why: Bargain! 「太贵了」, 「便宜一点」, a price of your own — 「二十块行吗？」 — or 「算了」: walk away, and they may call you back.

nodes.translate: All right — the coin is yours!
Hello! Have a look!

nodes.say: 天热了！买一个扇子吧！三十块。
nodes.translate: It's getting hot! Buy a fan! Thirty.
nodes.why: Bargain! 「太贵了」, 「便宜一点」, a price of your own — 「二十块行吗？」 — or 「算了」: walk away, and they may call you back.

nodes.translate: All right — here's your fan! Thank you!
Hello! Hot today, isn't it?

nodes.say: 鼻烟壶！很小，很漂亮！一百二。
nodes.translate: A snuff bottle! Tiny and beautiful! A hundred and twenty.
nodes.why: 一百二 is how the market says 一百二十 (120). Bargain: 「太贵了」, 「八十块行吗？」, or 「算了」 and walk away.

nodes.say: 好吧……鼻烟壶是你的了。谢谢！
nodes.translate: Oh well… the snuff bottle is yours. Thank you!
All my things are beautiful!

nodes.say: 你有铜钱？我看看……八块，卖不卖？
nodes.translate: You have a copper coin? Let me see… eight yuan — will you sell?
nodes.why: Now you are the seller: 「太少了」, 「多一点吧」, 「十五块行吗？」 — or 「算了」, and he may call you back. 好 sells.

nodes.say: 好，这个铜钱是我的了！谢谢！
nodes.translate: Good — this coin is mine now! Thank you!
Hello! Have you got something to sell?

steps.now: The book-seller at 潘家园 has an old map of Beijing — bargain for it.

legend.zh: 很久以前，每年的最后一个晚上，年兽会来村子里。人们发现，年兽怕红色，怕声音。所以过年的时候，人们贴红纸，放鞭炮。
legend.en: Long ago, on the last night of every year, the Nian beast came to the villages. People found it feared the colour red and loud noise — so at New Year they put up red paper and set off firecrackers.

befriend.en: Bargain it free from the stall.

idioms.meaning: better late than never: fix the problem after the first loss

story.zh: 一个人的羊圈坏了，狼进来，吃了一只羊。朋友说：“快修羊圈！”他没修。第二天，又少了一只羊。他马上修好了羊圈，以后羊再也没少。
story.en: A man's sheep pen had a hole; a wolf got in and took a sheep. His friend said, 'Mend it!' He didn't — and lost another. Then he mended it at once, and lost no more.
